Definition: a large public building, such as a palace or temple
BiblicalUsage: I take hêykâl to mean palace, temple, nave, sanctuary, nothing more and nothing less. It occurs 76 times, and 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel show it doing ordinary work in ordinary sentences. The Bible uses plain words plainly, and this is one of them.
TheologicalSignificance: hêykâl matters to me because God put His name in the temple so His people would know where to find Him. My position is that Scripture does not hide its meaning from honest readers.
RelatedEvents: Calling of Samuel; Hezekiah and Sennacherib's Invasion
